newsitem.title: GERMANY: Horlick eyes more talks with Deutsche in Frankfurt.
newsitem.headline: Horlick eyes more talks with Deutsche in Frankfurt.

text.p: Nicola Horlick said on Saturday she wished to pursue talks with the Frankfurt-based Deutsche Bank officials she met on Friday to discuss her departure from Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM).
In a telephone interview from her London home, the fund manager told Reuters, "We wish to continue the dialogue with the people in Germany. I want to see this settled as soon as possible."
Horlick, 35, who had been head of the British pension fund business at MGAM, said she would probably also have to negotiate with Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Deutsche's London-based investment arm.
"I think that's inevitable. After all they were my employers," she said. However she added: "I don't trust the Morgan Grenfell people and I thought I got a fair hearing in Germany."
Horlick was suspended last Tuesday pending the outcome of an internal investigation into what Deutsche Morgan Grenfell described as a "potential breach of contract."

The dispute is believed to revolve around allegations she tried to take a number of her MGAM team with her in a move to Dutch bank ABN Amro. Horlick has described this move by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell as "constructive dismissal."

Horlick held a two-hour meeting with one of Deutsche Bank's internal lawyers and a senior executive from its human resources division at Deutsche's Frankfurt headquarters on Friday, having flown in from London on an impromptu trip to seek a meeting with management board members.

Although she failed to meet the bank's top executives, Horlick said on leaving that meeting that she was "impressed" with the negotiators' attitude and later said she was upset to hear that Deutsche Morgan Grenfell had described the interview as a courtesy gesture.
Neither of the executives Horlick met on Friday could be reached on Saturday for comment.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell had said late on Friday that matters relating to Horlick's former employment should be addressed to MGAM rather than Deutsche.

Horlick said she had not yet spoken to her lawyer on Saturday but would do so during the course of the day. She said, "All I want to do now is put this matter in the hands of my lawyers and try to go on."
Horlick also said she wanted to reduce her exposure to the media and said she hoped she would not be making any more comments after today.
"They (the reporters) are camped this minute on my doorstep and I hope they won't be for much longer."
